GOVERN 1.1.reason: Legal and regulatory requirements for AI apply to builders and users alike.

GOVERN 1.2.reason: Both roles integrate trustworthy-AI characteristics into their own policies and procedures.

GOVERN 1.3.reason: Risk-tolerance-based depth of risk management applies to both; its impact-assessment mechanics sit with intended use for builders and with use context for users.

GOVERN 1.4.reason: Documentation policies cover purpose, scope and limitations for builders and a documentation inventory of AI in use for consumers.

GOVERN 1.5.reason: Periodic review, monitoring ownership and incident-response policy apply to both, with post-release monitoring for builders and incident handling for users.

GOVERN 1.6.reason: Builders inventory the models they build and release; consumers inventory the AI in use, which is also where unapproved use is found.

GOVERN 1.7.reason: Decommissioning is deprecation and withdrawal of a release for builders and retirement of an AI use, with fallback to a manual process, for consumers.

GOVERN 2.1.reason: Documented roles and lines of communication for AI risk apply to any org with AI.

GOVERN 2.2.reason: AI risk training for personnel and partners applies to builders and users.

GOVERN 2.3.reason: Executive responsibility for AI risk decisions applies to both roles.

GOVERN 3.1.reason: Who takes part in AI risk decisions (diversity of disciplines and backgrounds) can be asked of both.

GOVERN 3.2.reason: Defined roles for human-AI configurations and oversight apply to both; builders design the oversight, users operate and review outputs.

GOVERN 4.1.reason: A challenge and safety-first culture is asked about in the same way for both roles.

GOVERN 4.2.reason: Impact assessment policy applies to both: builders assess intended and foreseeable use, consumers assess their own uses.

GOVERN 4.3.reason: Practices to enable testing, identify incidents and share information apply to builders (evaluation, post-release) and users (validation, incident handling).

GOVERN 5.1.reason: Builders take feedback from recipients and affected people on a release; consumers take it from users and affected people of their own uses.

GOVERN 5.2.reason: Risk tolerance and approve, conditionally approve or reject decisions apply to releasing a model for builders and to approving an AI use for consumers.

GOVERN 6.1.reason: Third-party AI, data and IP risk policy: builders for base models and components, consumers for vendor AI and embedded features.

GOVERN 6.2.reason: Contingency for third-party failures covers base-model change or withdrawal for builders and vendor AI failure with a fallback for consumers.

MANAGE 1.1.reason: The go or no-go decision on whether the system meets its purpose is a release decision for builders and a use decision, with evidence from testing, for consumers.

MANAGE 1.2.reason: Prioritising risk treatment by impact and likelihood applies to both roles.

MANAGE 1.3.reason: Documented responses (mitigate, transfer, avoid, accept) to high-priority AI risks apply to both roles.

MANAGE 1.4.reason: Builders disclose residual risk and limits to downstream acquirers; consumers document the residual risk of their own use for the people it affects.

MANAGE 2.1.reason: Resourcing risk management and weighing non-AI alternatives applies to both roles.

MANAGE 2.2.reason: Controls that sustain a deployed system include security countermeasures in the build and serving stack for builders, and data handling and authenticated, limited access for consumers.

MANAGE 2.3.reason: Responding to a newly found risk needs monitoring and drift detection (both) and the ability to deactivate and recover (consumers act on it in use, builders in the release).

MANAGE 2.4.reason: Superseding, disengaging or deactivating a system is withdrawal or rollback of a release for builders and suspension of an AI use for consumers.

MANAGE 3.1.reason: Monitoring third-party AI risks: upstream models and components for builders, vendor AI for consumers.

MANAGE 3.2.reason: Tracking pre-trained models as third-party risk applies to builders on a base model and to consumers who fine-tune or run a pre-trained model.

MANAGE 4.1.reason: Post-deployment monitoring, appeal and override, and incident response apply to both: builders monitor releases, consumers monitor and handle problems in use.

MANAGE 4.2.reason: Continual improvement is change management of releases for builders and re-validation of the AI in use for consumers.

MANAGE 4.3.reason: Builders keep an issue intake and version history of what they release; consumers track and communicate incidents and errors in their own use.

MAP 1.1.reason: Documenting purpose, context and impacts applies to both: intended and foreseeable uses for builders, each AI use for consumers.

MAP 1.2.reason: Interdisciplinary participation in establishing context can be asked of both roles.

MAP 1.3.reason: Checking the AI purpose against mission and values applies to builders and to consumers choosing uses.

MAP 1.4.reason: Defining the business value or context of use applies to both roles.

MAP 1.5.reason: Documented organisational risk tolerance applies to both roles.

MAP 1.6.reason: Eliciting system requirements and making design decisions is the builder's work; a consumer's equivalent is covered by use context under MAP 1.x and procurement under GOVERN 6.

MAP 2.1.reason: Builders define the task and method of the model; consumers record the task each AI in use supports in their inventory.

MAP 2.2.reason: Documenting knowledge limits, human oversight of outputs and the system's connections to networks and other systems applies to both; what the AI can reach and act on is the access question.

MAP 2.3.reason: Experimental design, data collection and selection and construct validation are builder work; consumer validation before use is covered under MEASURE 2.x.

MAP 3.1.reason: Examining benefits of intended functionality applies to builders and to consumers deciding on a use.

MAP 3.2.reason: Examining costs and harms of expected or realised AI errors applies to both roles.

MAP 3.3.reason: Scoping of intended use is the builder's duty; a consumer's use context is covered under MAP 1.x.

MAP 3.4.reason: Builders define operator proficiency and provide training material and limits to recipients; consumers ensure the people operating the AI are competent and trained.

MAP 3.5.reason: Human oversight processes apply to both: designed oversight for builders, review and approval of AI outputs and actions for consumers.

MAP 4.1.reason: Mapping legal and IP risk of components covers third-party data, software and models for builders and vendor AI terms and contracts for consumers.

MAP 4.2.reason: Internal controls for third-party components: builders vet upstream material, consumers apply procurement, security and privacy controls to vendor AI and where it runs.

MAP 5.1.reason: Likelihood and magnitude of impacts is assessed by builders (with red teaming) and by consumers for their own uses.

MAP 5.2.reason: Engagement with affected parties and integrating their feedback applies to both roles.

MEASURE 1.1.reason: Choosing and documenting risk metrics applies to builders (evaluation and robustness) and consumers (validation of the AI in use).

MEASURE 1.2.reason: Regularly reassessing whether metrics and controls are effective applies to both roles.

MEASURE 1.3.reason: Independent assessors who are not front-line developers apply to builders; consumers use independent reviewers or domain experts in validating a use.

MEASURE 2.1.reason: Documenting test sets, metrics and tools applies to builders and to consumers validating AI before and during use.

MEASURE 2.2.reason: Human-subject evaluations and building representative test datasets are builder work; consumer fairness is asked through use context under MEASURE 2.11.

MEASURE 2.3.reason: Measuring performance under conditions like deployment applies to builders and to consumers testing in their own context.

MEASURE 2.4.reason: Monitoring behaviour in production applies to builders (post-release) and consumers (the AI in use).

MEASURE 2.5.reason: Demonstrating validity and reliability and documenting limits applies to builders and to consumers before relying on a use.

MEASURE 2.6.reason: Safety evaluation and the ability to fail safely apply to both: stress testing for builders, validation and the ability to stop or fall back for consumers.

MEASURE 2.7.reason: Security and resilience testing applies to both: red teaming and protection against model extraction for builders, hostile-input testing and authenticated, limited access for consumers.

MEASURE 2.8.reason: Transparency and accountability measurement needs audit logs of what the AI did and human override statistics, for builders and for consumers.

MEASURE 2.9.reason: Builders explain, validate and document the model (model cards); consumers apply it only through how outputs are interpreted and used.

MEASURE 2.10.reason: Privacy risk is asked as training-data privacy for builders and as what personal data reaches the AI, and how it is handled, for consumers.

MEASURE 2.11.reason: Fairness testing is builder work; consumers apply it through how outputs are used in decisions about people.

MEASURE 2.12.reason: Environmental impact of training and operating a model is assessed by the builder; a consumer's footprint is the vendor's and has no practice question.

MEASURE 2.13.reason: Evaluating whether TEVV metrics and processes work applies to builders and to consumers validating their uses.

MEASURE 3.1.reason: Tracking existing and emergent risks against baselines and feedback applies to both roles.

MEASURE 3.2.reason: Risk tracking where metrics are not yet available applies to both roles.

MEASURE 3.3.reason: Feedback and appeal channels: builders run issue intake for recipients; consumers give users a way to report problems and contest outcomes and track them.

MEASURE 4.1.reason: Connecting measurement to the deployment context and consulting end users applies to both roles.

MEASURE 4.2.reason: Validating trustworthiness results with domain experts and end users applies to both roles.

MEASURE 4.3.reason: Baselines and tracking performance improvements or declines applies to both roles.
